8fdf0faa0a.q: Why do only 6% of companies make real money on AI investments according to McKinsey research?
8fdf0faa0a.a: According to McKinsey's recent study of 1,700 companies, only 6% are making real money on AI. Those 6% who were really successful admit they redesigned how the work gets done. The key is understanding how work actually flows before implementing AI, rather than simply automating existing broken processes.

e1f7be1882.q: What is 'paving the cow path' in AI implementation and why is it ineffective?
e1f7be1882.a: Paving the cow path means automating existing processes without redesigning them first. In one example, an insurance benefits broker wanted to use AI to create the same three or four spreadsheets they manually created before. Instead, Genient showed them those spreadsheets weren't needed anymore—AI could triage their next best action automatically, eliminating four hours of manual data aggregation work entirely.

d93cbc1d71.q: What does Genient mean by 'Olympian worker' and how does AI automation require higher performance from employees?
d93cbc1d71.a: As AI removes boring administrative work from people's day-to-day tasks, workers must perform at higher cognitive levels—like Olympians running a 10-second hundred-meter dash. Not everyone will adjust to having less busy work and more high-value work. The reality is that automation of busy work will require more people to perform at higher levels, changing job descriptions and organizational charts, which presents a real change management challenge.

3fd71d90ab.q: How does Genient use anthropologists and psychologists before building AI software?
3fd71d90ab.a: Genient employs full-time anthropologists and psychologists who conduct qualitative research to understand broken processes before designers begin work using AI. This research phase ensures they understand the underlying motivations and behaviors of humans, which prevents building impressive software that doesn't address actual organizational and job description changes needed for success.

72d26880fe.q: What percentage of Americans view AI positively according to recent brand strategy research?
72d26880fe.a: Research from a brand strategist working with mid-cap companies showed that only 9% to 11% of Americans have a positive view of AI. This contrasts with actual use cases where AI is demonstrably good for society and the economy, indicating that public sentiment is heavily influenced by fear-based narratives rather than practical evidence of benefit.
